examples.text: Sie musste ihn mehrmals anschreiben, weil sie keine Antwort erhielt.

examples.english: She had to write to him several times, because she did not receive an answer.

to charge (something to someone's account)

examples.text: Er läßt schon wieder beim Laden anschreiben.
examples.translation: He had it charged to his account again at the store.

examples.text: Ein hochwertiger Füller sollte sofort anschreiben.
examples.translation: A high-quality fountain-pen should write immediately.

examples.text: Der Vorstand des Sportvereines hat alle Mitglieder angeschrieben, um sie um Hilfe bei der Organisation des Kindersportfestes zu bitten.

examples.text: Vergessen Sie bitte nicht das Anschreiben zu unterschreiben, Fr. Müller.

glosses: einleitender Teil einer Bewerbung für eine Arbeitsstelle

examples.text: Für das Anschreiben gilt: Fassen Sie sich kurz.

glosses: substantivierte Form von anschreiben

examples.text: Das Anschreiben macht immer dann Sinn, wenn der Vertragspartner telefonisch nicht zu erreichen ist.
„Funktionen, wie das private Anschreiben einzelner Nutzer, […] sind über den kostenpflichtigen Abschluss der zwei verschiedenen Premium-Modelle verfügbar.“
„Das ganze Anschreiben gegen die Zocker hatte doch kaum etwas berwirkt.“

glosses: A letter or written communication that serves to introduce an accompanying document; especially, a letter that introduces a résumé or curriculum vitae.
A cover letter.

Con manchas similares a las letras en un papel.
Participio irregular de escribir.

glosses: Lettre courte et concise à destination d’une personne ayant la fonction de directeur des ressources humaines (une entreprise, une association, etc.) qui permet à un candidat (chercheur d’emploi, stagiaire, etc.) de montrer sa motivation et ses qualités en vue d’obtenir un poste ou un stage.

examples.text: Certains recruteurs se fient beaucoup à la graphologie pour connaître les candidats, et c’est pourquoi ils exigent des lettres de motivation manuscrites.
La lettre de motivation sans CV ne sert à rien, et le CV sans lettre de motivation ne sert guère mieux.

glosses: für alle lesbar auf eine Fläche (Tafel, Wand oder Ähnliches) schreiben

examples.text: Das täglich wechselnde Menü wird immer sorgfältig auf einer kleinen Tafel angeschrieben.

glosses: (eine geschuldete Geldsumme für eine spätere Bezahlung) aufschreiben, schriftlich festhalten

examples.text: Wenn ich meinen Geldbeutel mal vergessen habe, schreibt der Wirt meines Stammlokals meine Bierchen eben an.
Beim Skatspielen schreibt man normalerweise die Punkte an und am Ende wird abgerechnet, beim Schafkopfen wird jedes Spiel gleich bar bezahlt.

glosses: an jemanden schreiben, sich mit einem Schreiben an jemanden wenden, jemanden schriftlich kontaktieren

examples.text: Wenn du deine Versicherung telefonisch nicht erreichen kannst, musst du sie eben anschreiben.

glosses: als Autor mit der Veröffentlichung von Texten ausdauernd gegen jemanden/etwas vorgehen, ankämpfen

examples.text: „Jede politische Entscheidung, die denen nicht passt, empfinden diese Menschen als diktatorische Zumutung. Und weil die Medien nicht in ihrem Sinne dagegen anschreiben, suchen sie sich ihren eigenen Echoraum, und das ist Facebook.“

glosses: To form letters, words or symbols on a surface in order to communicate.

examples.text: The pupil wrote his name on the paper.
Your son has been writing on the wall.

glosses: To be the author of (a book, article, poem, etc.).

examples.text: My uncle writes newspaper articles for The Herald.

Thus, when he drew up instructions in lawyer language[…]; his clerks, however, understood him very well. If he had written a love letter, or a farce, or a ballade, or a story, no one, either clerks, or friends, or compositors, would have understood anything but a word here and a word there.

Since I had started to break down all my writing and get rid of all facility and try to make instead of describe, writing had been wonderful to do. But it was very difficult, and I did not know how I would ever write anything as long as a novel. It often took me a full morning of work to write a paragraph.

glosses: To send written information to.

examples.text: (UK) Please write to me when you get there.
(US) Please write me when you get there.

glosses: To show (information, etc) in written form.

examples.text: Ghana's motto, writ large on the gleaming white Independence Arch that overlooks the Atlantic in Accra, is "Freedom and Justice."
The due day of the homework is written in the syllabus.

The route passes over low-lying land, the only item of note being the Cerebos salt works at Greatham, where one may catch a glimpse of the smart black diesel locomotive emblazoned with the firm's name writ large.

glosses: To convey a fact to someone via writing.

examples.text: Jimmy wrote me that he needs more money.
Do you know, one man actually wrote me he thought he could almost shave with the back of the blade, the lather "mellowed" his beard so.

glosses: To be an author.

examples.text: I write for a living.
I said that I did not believe anyone could write any way except the very best he could write without destroying his talent.

glosses: To record data mechanically or electronically.

examples.text: The computer writes to the disk faster than it reads from it.

glosses: To fill in, to complete using words.

examples.text: I was very anxious to know my score after I wrote the test.
Kúnlé had failed biology and chemistry, key requirements for admission into any medical school in the country. Kúnlé’s father wanted him to write the exams again.

glosses: To impress durably; to imprint; to engrave.

examples.text: truth written on the heart

14 For when the Gentiles which haue not the Law, doe by nature the things contained in the Law: these hauing not the Law, are a Law vnto themselues,
15 Which shew the worke of the Law written in their hearts, their conscience also bearing witnesse, and their thoughts the meane while accusing, or else excusing one another:

glosses: To make known by writing; to record; to prove by one's own written testimony; often used reflexively.

examples.text:
Thoſe walled garriſons will I ſubdue,
And write my ſelfe great Lord of Affrica:
So from the Eaſt vnto the furtheſt Weſt,
Shall Tamburlaine extend his puiſant arme.

He who writes himself Martyr by his own inscription, is like an ill painter, who by writing on a shapeless picture which he hath drawn, is fain to tell passengers what shape it is, which else no man could imagine.

glosses: To sell (an option or other derivative).
To paint a religious icon or a pysanka egg.
The act or style of writing.

examples.text: The pen also gives a better write than the ordinary counter pen. The ink stand cannot be stolen, for it is fastened to the counter or desk.

glosses: The operation of storing data, as in memory or onto disk.

examples.text: How many writes per second can this hard disk handle?
In other words, the system can do 1200 reads per second with no writes, the average write is twice as slow as the average read, and the relationship is linear.

glosses: Used other than figuratively or idiomatically: see write, down.

examples.text: I can't write down in the basement; it's cold there and my fingers cramp and get stiff.

glosses: To produce or set (something) down in writing; to record something.
To write (something) in a simple or condescending style.

examples.text: Good heavens, I can't write down to the level of the vulgar public!

glosses: To make a downward adjustment in the value of an asset.
To condemn in writing; to document the faults, offenses, or wrongdoing of.

examples.text: By 1859, D. Morier Evans was exhibiting [George] Hudson as the principal character in his rogues' gallery entitled "Facts, Failures and Frauds"; and at the hands of modern economic historians he has been written down as a common swindler.
